# Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Stops a passive proxy session.

## SYNTAX

```
Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy [-Name] <string> [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy cmdlet stops the passive proxy session named in -Name, or each session piped from Get-ZbxPassiveProxyStatus: it closes the listener, frees the port and drops the configuration and values the session held. -WhatIf shows which session it would stop. It writes nothing.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Stop a passive proxy

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1' -Version '7.0' -Port 30160
Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy'
```

-Name (position 0) is the name Start-ZbxPassiveProxy gave the session.

### Example 2: Stop every passive proxy session of this runspace

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1' -Version '7.0' -Port 30160
Get-ZbxPassiveProxyStatus | Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy
```

Each session piped from Get-ZbxPassiveProxyStatus binds -Name.

## PARAMETERS

### -Name

The session's name (the -Name it was started with).

### -WhatIf

Shows what would happen if the command ran. The command does not run.

### -Confirm

Prompts for confirmation before the command changes anything.
